exposure: age gap to the nearest older sibling
outcome: human parechovirus other than type 3 (non-HPeV-3) infections
cohort: The study included all children under 5 years of age in Denmark who had HPeV infections detected between 2009 and 2012.
finding: Having a slightly older sibling significantly increases the risk for severe neonatal HPeV infections, particularly HPeV-3, with secondborn children and shorter age gaps showing a higher risk.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was not associated with the risk of HPeV infections.
